description.narrative:
ASSOJ, a Mozambican youth-led social enterprise founded in 2020, has trained 1,780 youth, placed 120 in jobs, and achieved a 45% business survival rate. This project strengthens BOOSTAR, Clube Empreendedor, and Hub de Inovação to raise earned revenue from €20,000to €50,000/year, cut donor dependency to 50%, and expand impact from 50 to 500 youth annually, 60% women, using a cross-subsidy model.
This project creates sustainable impact beyond 12 months through five pathways: individual empowerment, cooperatives, ecosystems, financial sustainability, and systemic change. Youth gain permanent skills, launch viable businesses, and increase incomes, creating jobs and breaking poverty cycles. Cooperatives build lasting collective power through shared assets, reinvested profits, and democratic ownership. Networks and alumni systems sustain mentorship and market access, while government integration enables national scale. ASSOJ’s revenue model reduces donor dependency and guarantees continuity via cross-subsidy. Together, these mechanisms create a self-sustaining ecosystem.

participating-org.narrative:
ASSOCIAÇÃO PARA EMPODERAMENTO JUVENIL (ASSOJ) is a Mozambican youth-led social enterprise founded in 2020 to transform the economicprospects of marginalized young people through integrated entrepreneurship, employability, and civic engagement programs.
VISION: To be a national reference in forming an empowered, active, and productive youth generation that drives sustainable community development across Mozambique.
MISSION: To transmit the best international entrepreneurship experience while adapting it to Mozambican realities, creating pathways for youth to transition from economic vulnerability to productive citizenship. We combine social mission with income-generating activities, ensuring long-term sustainability while prioritizing impact on marginalized communities.
CORE OBJECTIVES: - Promote youth entrepreneurship through business training, mentorship, and advocacy for enabling environments - Establishan inclusive socio-economic system capable of guaranteeing inclusion, sustainability, and economic competitiveness - Capacitate young entrepreneurs and advocate for ecosystem improvements that support youth business development - Train communities and youth in business management and income-generation project design - Provide assistance to vulnerable youth - Conduct workshops and seminars on community development, psychosocial, and educational topics - Promote youth exchange of experiences and inter-organizational learning nationally and internationally - Intervene in community development initiatives
ORGANIZATIONAL VALUES: - Youth Leadership: Young people (18-35) constitute 100% of our governance and implementation teams - Inclusion First: Prioritizing marginalized youth—especially young women, rural migrants, and out-of-school youth - Mission-Driven Sustainability: Combining social impact with revenue generation, ensuring surpluses reinvest in expanding access for the most vulnerable - Evidence-Based Impact: Using data to track outcomes, demonstrate results, and inform policy - Community Ownership: Building local capacity and leadership rather than creating dependency - Collaborative Innovation: Learning from international best practices while adapting to Mozambican context
Since 2020, ASSOJ has trained 1,780 youth across multiple programs, inserted 120 young people into productive employment, and achieved a 45% business incubation success rate—demonstrating our model's effectiveness in creating sustainable economic opportunities for Mozambican youth.
